text:
sophie: Heads-up  enterprise customer (AtlasCare) asked for a "quantize+discount" add-on: they will accept model variants quantized to 4-bit for 30% lower price on served tokens. Want product, eng, finance + legal alignment before commit.

rahul: Quick clarifying Q: are they asking for a permanent price tier for quantized variants or a pilot discount tied to specific routes?

carmen: Sales says pilot: per-route opt-in. AtlasCare wants a 30% token-price discount if they opt into our aggressive quantization profile, no extra commit. They care about cost, not minor quality drop.

greg: Engineering: major concerns  some models lose safety/QA characteristics at low-bit quant. Need per-model evals, fallback policies and automatic quality monitoring. We should never let quantized variant be default for sessions where customers request strict fidelity.

financebot: From finance: discounts at 30% materially change unit economics if adoption scales. Need a pilot floor and a usage cap. Recommend: pilot discount up to 250M quantized tokens/month, then tiered discount or revert to standard price. Also require a one-time enablement fee to cover evals.

legalbot: Legal: customers often try to push discounted artifacts into SLA claims. We should add contract language: "Quantized variants are best-effort and are excluded from latency/quality SLA claims; use at customer's discretion." Also require an explicit opt-in clause.

sophie: Product proposal: add `quantization_addon` as route-level add-on with fields: `profile` (e.g., q4_0/q4_1), `discount_pct`, `monthly_cap_tokens`, `fallback_policy`. Example (informal):
```json
{"quantization_addon": {"profile":"q4_0","discount_pct":30,"monthly_cap_tokens":250000000,"fallback_policy":"auto-fallback-to-full"}}
```
This would let runtime know billing/behavior.

rahul: Implementation notes: we must tag requests so we can attribute quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim) and emit `quantized.variant_used` events. Also need canary rollout per customer, not global.

carmen: Customer wants visibility: a Console tile showing quantized token usage, % quality regressions, and remaining discount cap. Important for AtlasCare's procurement.

greg: Runtime fallback options: 1) auto-fallback to full-precision variant on high hallucination score, 2) auto-fallback if tail latency > threshold after quantization, 3) manual opt-out. Need a runbook and deterministic triggers.

opsbot: Suggest trigger heuristics: hallucination_score > 0.6 for 5 min OR p95 latency degrade > 40% for 3min -> route shifts traffic to full model variant for that route; record event `quantized.fallback`.

financebot: Billing phrasing draft: "Quantization discount: 30% discount on token rates for requests served by agreed quantization profiles up to monthly cap of 250M tokens. Usage above cap billed at standard rates. A one-time enablement fee of $X applies. Redwood reserves right to revoke discount for safety/regulatory reasons."

legalbot: Replace "revoke" with "suspend" and include explicit causes (safety incident, regulatory request, sustained quality regressions per metric thresholds). Also add audit rights for Redwood to verify opt-in.

rahul: Quality monitoring plan: 1) baseline eval before pilot with held-out prompts, 2) daily sampled evaluation with automated regression alerts, 3) rollback if regression > 5% on agreed metrics for 3 consecutive days.

sophie: Launch criteria (product): 1) eng spec PR for `quantization_addon` and runtime tagging, 2) pre-pilot eval report for AtlasCare models, 3) Console tile + billing export, 4) legal addendum + finance floor, 5) runbook with deterministic fallback triggers.

carmen: Sales asks for a 90-day pilot start window. Is that realistic?

greg: Tight but doable if models are already in catalog and we have eval infra. If customer has custom model, needs additional eval time. Recommend 6 weeks for standard-model pilot.

financebot: Also recommend telemetry SLA: 48h accuracy on usage reports so invoices are correct for discounted tokens.

legalbot: One more contract point: ensure discounted tokens cannot be used to claim model quality parity. Add explicit disclaimer in pilot addendum.

rahul: Dev plan: will add event schema `quantized.request` with fields route_id, profile, tokens, quality_score_estimate; emit `quantized.fallback` with reason_code. Carmen, will you own Console wireframe?

carmen: Yes, will mock minimal tile: usage bar, remaining cap, recent fallback events, and download CSV link. Will post by Fri.

sophie: Action items recap: 1) Greg -> eng spec + fallback PR by Wed. 2) Rahul -> telemetry/event schema + eval harness run by Thu. 3) Carmen -> Console mock + CSV export spec by Fri. 4) Finance -> finalize pilot floor/enablement fee by Tue. 5) Legal -> draft addendum + disclaimers by Wed. 6) Sophie -> decision after eval results.

greg: I'll include a canary schedule: start 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% (5 days each) with automated rollback.

carmen: AtlasCare specifically asked for a CSV with daily token breakdown and a weekly quality summary. Finance, can we accommodate weekly CSV?

financebot: Weekly CSV ok for pilot, but escalate to monthly for general availability. We'll include sample template in invoice flow.

sophie: Risks noted: 1) quality regressions impact trust; 2) accounting complexity; 3) possible customers over-indexing on discount vs SLA expectations. We'll mitigate via explicit opt-in, console visibility, and runbook.

legalbot: We'll prepare the addendum with opt-in, excluded SLAs, suspension triggers, and audit language. Expect draft by Wed EOD.

rahul: I'll create INF ticket and link eval artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9999

opsbot: INF-9999 created and assigned to greg, rahul, carmen  due 2026-06-08.

sophie: Thanks all  I'll coordinate customer comms once PRs and evals land.

carmen: tagging @atlascare-sales to set expectations.

end of thread.
